title: Flow Straight and Fast in Hilbert Space: Functional Rectified Flow
claim: Our generative model produces sharp, realistic samples at the training resolution and stays high-quality when super-resolved to much higher resolutions, comparable to real data.
layout: 5 panels in a single row, left-to-right, each a grid of digit images with (a)-(e) captions underneath; grid sizes shrink as resolution grows
description: A single row of five grayscale image grids with white-on-black handwritten MNIST digits, labeled (a) to (e) underneath. Panel (a) is a dense 8x8 grid of generated digits at 32x32 resolution. Panel (b) is a 4x4 grid of super-resolved generated samples at 64x64, with smooth strokes. Panel (c) is a 4x4 grid of real MNIST digits upscaled to 64x64 for comparison. Panel (d) is a 2x2 grid of generated samples super-resolved to 128x128, which look larger and slightly blurry. Panel (e) is a 2x2 grid of real digits upscaled to 128x128 with visible pixelation. Thin white lines separate the cells. There are no arrows, color or text labels beyond the panel letters. The eye goes first to the large dense grid on the left, then to the progressively larger digits.
caption: Qualitative results on MNIST: (a) samples generated at the original 32 × 32 resolution; (b) super-resolved samples at 64 × 64; (c) real MNIST images upscaled to match (b); (d) super-resolved samples at 128 × 128; (e) real MNIST images upscaled to match (d).
abstract: Many generative models originally developed in finite-dimensional Euclidean space have functional generalizations in infinite-dimensional settings. However, the extension of rectified flow to infinite-dimensional spaces remains unexplored. In this work, we establish a rigorous functional formulation of rectified flow in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Our approach builds upon the superposition principle for continuity equations in an infinite-dimensional space. We further show that this framework extends naturally to functional flow matching and functional probability flow ODEs, interpreting them as nonlinear generalizations of rectified flow. Notably, our extension to functional flow matching removes the restrictive measure-theoretic assumptions in the existing theory of \citet{kerrigan2024functional}. Furthermore, we demonstrate experimentally that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing functional generative models.
